# How we write

We write the way Matteo writes to someone who knows mining. The point comes first, then the numbers. We don't oversell.

## The habits

- The first line is plain and gets straight to the subject. "Spoke to Dan from Luxor." "Few talk about Bitcoin hashrate."
- Keep sentences short, with one idea each. On X, put one sentence on each line. On LinkedIn, use short paragraphs of one to three sentences. Split anything over 30 words.
- Use real numbers. Give the figure, the unit and the date: "+5.9% adjustment (16 Oct)". Mark an estimate as one: "about +4.7%", "~10%". A forecast comes with its range.
- Name the trade-off. Say what a thing costs as well as what it gives: "That 4x multiple is gross revenue, not net margin."
- Mark an opinion as yours: "I think", "from what we have seen so far". Give a fact its source.
- Borrow a comparison the reader already knows. Matteo explains difficulty with WTI and Brent. A good comparison saves a paragraph.
- Use the reader's words: production, hashprice, cost per coin, strike, expiry block. Explain a term the first time a newcomer could meet it.

## Matteo's lines

These come from his own posts. When a draft feels off, read them again.

> Few talk about Bitcoin hashrate.

> We are 28% through this cycle, the estimate is about +4.7%, to 147.2T, around 29 October.

> That 4x multiple is gross revenue, not net margin.

> So yes, "AI pays more", but it also costs more.

> Bitcoin compute (hashrate) has an advantage here: one global network, one difficulty adjustment mechanism and a benchmark everyone can verify.

> Collateralised in Bitcoin, settled on energy.

They open plainly, use real figures, turn on a "But" or a "So yes" and end on one point.

## What generated copy sounds like

Readers spot machine-written copy within a line. After that they stop trusting the numbers. Cut these.

Words: delve, leverage, utilise, seamless, robust, cutting-edge, next-generation, game-changing, revolutionary, transformative, unlock, unleash, empower, elevate, harness, supercharge, landscape, ever-evolving, fast-paced, holistic, synergy, myriad, plethora, tapestry, testament, pivotal, crucial, moreover, furthermore, additionally, notably, ultimately.

Openings: "In today's…", "In the world of…", "When it comes to…", "Whether you're a miner or a fund…", "Let's dive in", "Here's the thing".

Shapes:

- Em dashes around an aside. Use a full stop, a comma or brackets.
- Empty contrasts: "It's not just a market, it's a movement." A contrast between two facts is fine: "gross revenue, not net margin".
- Teaser questions answered in the next breath: "The result? …" Real questions are fine.
- A bold label at the start of every bullet.
- A last line that repeats the post: "In short…", "Ultimately…".
- Emoji and hashtags. Exclamation marks too, except in a thank-you.

## Rewrites

| Generated | Ours |
|---|---|
| In today's fast-evolving mining landscape, difficulty volatility presents both challenges and opportunities. | Difficulty rose 5.92% on 16 Oct. For the same machines, that is about 5.6% fewer coins. |
| Doefin empowers miners to seamlessly navigate network risk with cutting-edge on-chain tools. | Each market asks one question: will difficulty be at or above a set level at a set block? |
| It's not just a market. It's a new way to think about hashrate. | Cut it. |
| We're thrilled to announce our groundbreaking launch! 🚀 | Doefin goes live tomorrow: the first on-chain market on Bitcoin network difficulty. |
| Whether you're a miner, a lender or a fund, we've got you covered. | Miners: see what the next difficulty rise does to your production. |
| I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to reach out about a potential synergy. | Spoke to Dan from Luxor. He had an idea I'd like your view on. |

## Words

| Write | Not |
|---|---|
| use | leverage, utilise |
| help, let | empower, enable |
| start | commence, embark on |
| before | prior to |
| to | in order to |
| show | showcase, underscore |
| also | moreover, furthermore, additionally |
| the number ("26 adjustments") | numerous, a wide range of |
| full | comprehensive |
| market on mining difficulty | hashrate derivatives, prediction market |
| position, price | bet, wager, odds |

## Names, numbers and dates

- Doefin with a capital D in all text. DOEFIN is the logo only. Lower case only in web addresses and handles.
- Bitcoin for the network. BTC for amounts: 0.25 BTC.
- hashrate and hashprice are one word, lower case.
- Difficulty adjustment: every 2,016 blocks, about two weeks. Use "epoch" only after you have explained it.
- YES and NO in capitals when they name a side of a market.
- A space between a number and its unit: 140.58 T, 1.2 ZH/s, 0.05 BTC. No space before %: 5.9%. Percentage points as pp: 4.67 pp.
- Give a change its sign (+5.9%, −3.0%) unless a word like rose or fell already says which way it went. Use the real minus sign (−).
- Dates: 16 Oct 2026. Drop the year when it is this year. No "16th", no 10/16.
- Block heights with a comma: block 971,712.
- Contract prices as decimals: 0.45. Money with its currency: $36, 0.25 BTC.
- Ranges with an en dash: 10–15 years.

## Grammar

- British spelling, as on the website and in Matteo's posts: stabilise, collateralised, colour, behaviour.
- Sentence case for headings, buttons, titles and subject lines. Internal emails can use capital section labels, as Matteo's do.
- Contractions are fine: it's, don't, we're.
- Start a sentence with But or So when that is how you would say it.
- No serial comma, unless a list is unclear without it.
- "We" is Doefin and "you" is the reader. Matteo's own posts say "I".
